approachQuestion.prompt:
Summarize Consecutive States

A finite acyclic singly linked list contains integer state codes. Return a new singly linked list of records (code,count), one per maximal consecutive run of equal codes, in encounter order. Preserve the entire input unchanged; no result node may be an input node. Input is head; 0 <= n <= 200000. Counts fit in a machine word, and creating or writing one fixed-size record has constant cost.

Input: [7,7,2,7,7,7]. Output: [(7,2),(2,1),(7,3)] -> null.
Input: null. Output: null. Input: [3]. Output: [(3,1)] -> null.

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Copy every input code into an array, scan that array to compute consecutive runs, and append fresh result records.
options.feedback: This preserves the run semantics, but copying all codes adds storage that streaming does not need.

options.text: Count each distinct code across the entire input and return one record per distinct code.
options.feedback: [7,2,7] needs three run records, not a single combined count for 7.

options.text: Append a new record for a run only when a different code is encountered; return immediately at end without flushing.
options.feedback: Input [3] produces no result record even though its final run must be returned.

options.text: Walk the input with the current run code and count. When a different code arrives, append a new record for the finished run and start the next. Append the final run after traversal; return null for empty input.
options.feedback: A run ends exactly at a change of adjacent code; only its code and count are needed until that boundary.

feedback.reason: A run ends exactly at a change of adjacent code; only its code and count are needed until that boundary.

Consecutive equal codes form one record; the same code in separated runs needs separate records. Emit the final pending run after traversal and return no record for an empty input.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (acm-b15-21-target), regardless of your Q1 choice. Here n. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Count each node allocation, link access, identity/value comparison and machine-word operation as constant work. Include all temporary collections and call frames; exclude supplied nodes and the final returned output only. Copying or allocating k records costs k operations. No hash-table, amortized-operation or tail-call assumptions are used.

options.explanation: This pair does not describe the fixed method. Every input node is read once and at most n output records are allocated. All-equal input still requires reading n codes to establish the count. The returned run records are output, so their allocation costs time but not auxiliary space. A fixed code/count and result-tail references suffice, without recursion.
